doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Collecting records and the Chautauqua party's closing number
summary: Records given by performers, and the emotional Haggart 'South Rampart Street Parade' at Chautauqua.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well over the years, I would imagine you’ve bought records, collected things, is that something you’re pretty happy with?

Yes. And many of them have been given to me by performers — and so many. I hate to mention any person because there are so many that I’d say he didn’t mention me and I’m not trying to mention names because there are so many that are just as dear and precious, © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -16-
and some of them are here at this party. It’s always an emotional experience. One of the exciting things — you were at ...

Chautauqua party. The emotional minute of that thing was the last time when the big band played and the closing thing was Bob Haggart’s “South Rampart Street Parade.” And they played that, I could just cry that was so good. I’ve known Bob Haggart for 40 years. I knew him and his wife as a fan and becoming a friend. And I can never forget the way they played that one piece. It just dissolved me nearly. And he’s a remarkable person.
